newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ito En sees better earnings than forecast.
newsitem.headline: Ito En sees better earnings than forecast.

text.p: Leading Japanese tea manufacturer Ito En Ltd said on Wednesday it is likely to post better earnings for the business year to April 30 than it earlier forecast.
Company president Hachiro Honjo told Reuters that sales of its lucrative 500-ml plastic-bottle tea products had gained momentum, helped by unusually good weather in both January and February.

This factor, combined with rapid growth in sales of the firm"s Chinese tea of about 80 percent year-on-year, meant it would likely revise upward its earnings estimate for the current business year, he said.
However, he stopped short of saying to what extent the earnings forecast would increased.

In December, the company predicted a parent current profit of 6.3 billion yen for 1996/97, up 8.0 percent from the previous year. It forecast parent sales of 117 billion yen, up from actual sales of 105.62 billion yen in 1995/96. April would be negative for the company"s business, but the company had already taken measures to offset the loss, which is estimated to be 1.3 billion yen a year.

He said the company would basically keep the sales price of its canned drinks at 110 yen, but may raise prices on some value-added products. The company will, meanwhile, streamline its operations to cut costs, he said.

He said the company aims to boost its parent sales to 200 billion yen in 2001. "We can expect sales of around 170 billion yen (in 2001) even with our existing products, the rest is up to our future products," he said.
